name: Bedrock AgentCore Services
description: Hexagonal ports + adapters for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore stateful services — Memory (multi-turn + long-term recall), Gateway (APIs/Lambdas/MCP as MCP tools), and Identity (workload token + IdP claim bridge to UserContext). The application layer depends only on the ports; install @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-agentcore.

questions.prompt: Identity provider to bridge to UserContext?

checklist: Install the SDK (no manifest deps field — this is the only channel): npm install @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-agentcore
Provision the resources you enabled: `agentcore add memory --strategies SEMANTIC,SUMMARY` ; `agentcore add gateway` ; then `agentcore deploy`
Copy AGENTCORE_MEMORY_ID / AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL / AGENTCORE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_ARN from `agentcore status` into .env.local
Grant the runtime execution role access to the new Memory/Gateway resources (extend iam/agentcore-runtime-role.policy.json)
Merge the blocks in agentcore/agentcore-services.json into agentcore/agentcore.json (this template does not overwrite the runtime's file)
If using Identity: set AGENTCORE_IDP_DISCOVERY_URL and confirm idp-bridge.ts maps your IdP's claims onto UserContext (reuse an installed auth provider's mapping if present)
Gateway adapter is a minimal MCP-over-HTTP client — swap in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk if your Gateway needs the full session/initialize handshake
Wire each adapter behind its port at composition root; run your port-fake tests before hitting live AWS
